title: Private Subnet Instance Cannot Access Internet via NAT Gateway
symptom: EC2 instance in a private subnet cannot connect to external internet endpoints (yum, external APIs).
environment: AWS VPC with public subnet, private subnet, and NAT Gateway.

possible_causes.cause: NAT Gateway was mistakenly placed in the private subnet instead of the public subnet
possible_causes.evidence_needed: NAT Gateway subnet lacks route to Internet Gateway.
possible_causes.remediation: Deploy NAT Gateway in a public subnet that has an explicit route to an Internet Gateway.

possible_causes.cause: Private subnet route table missing default route to the NAT Gateway (0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxx)
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Private route table only contains local VPC CIDR route.
possible_causes.remediation: Add route 0.0.0.0/0 with target set to the NAT Gateway ID.

investigation_steps.title: Inspect Route Table Associated with Private Subnet
investigation_steps.explanation: Confirm private subnet routes 0.0.0.0/0 to nat-xxxxxxxx.

investigation_steps.title: Verify NAT Gateway Placement Subnet and Public Route
investigation_steps.explanation: Check which subnet hosts the NAT Gateway and verify that subnet's route table.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: NAT Gateway's subnet must have an igw-xxxx default route.

verification: From private instance: `curl -I https://checkip.amazonaws.com` returns successfully.
prevention: Use VPC Reachability Analyzer to validate end-to-end paths before going to production.
